sentences.text: Tylosaurus was a derived mosasaur with advanced traits including a fully aquatic lifestyle.
The largest species, T. rex, is estimated to have reached over 13 meters in length and weighed nearly 8.4 tonnes.
The largest known Tylosaurus skull belongs to the "Bunker" specimen and is estimated to be up to 1.63 meters long.
The frontal bone in Tylosaurus usually has a low midline crest, most prominent in T. proriger and moderately developed in T. saskatchewanensis and T. bernardi.
Tylosaurus possessed 2 premaxillary, 12 to 13 maxillary, 13 dentary, and 10 to 11 pterygoid teeth on each side of its skull.
The largest well-known Tylosaurus specimen is nicknamed "Bunker" and is housed at the University of Kansas Natural History Museum.
In 2026, researchers estimated the largest Tylosaurus specimen was 13.2 meters long, while the species generally ranged from 7.7 to 13.2 meters.
A 5-meter-long Tylosaurus had dermal scales measuring 3.3 mm, with an average of ninety scales per square inch on its underside.
A 1987 find revealed a T. proriger skeleton containing the stomach contents of a 2-meter-long mosasaur, a diving bird, a fish, and possibly a shark.
A 5-meter-long T. kansasensis holotype shows injuries indicating it was killed by a larger Tylosaurus in a fatal intraspecific combat.
Edward Drinker Cope presented a preliminary description of the type specimen in 1869, initially naming it Macrosaurus proriger.
Louis Dollo described the species Hainosaurus bernardi in 1885 based on a skeleton found in a phosphate quarry in the Ciply Basin of Mesvin, Belgium.
In 1804, the Lewis and Clark Expedition discovered a fossil skeleton along the Missouri River that was identified as a 45-foot-long fish.
Tylosaurus possessed an endothermic metabolism, a trait unlike nearly all modern squamates.
Dark coloration in Tylosaurus likely helped maintain elevated body temperatures in colder environments by increasing heat absorption.
Researchers suggest Tylosaurus may have rapidly filled an ecological niche left by the extinction of pliosaurs and the decline of polycotylids.
Juvenile Tylosaurus showed rapid growth in the first few years before slowing to a steady rate starting around year 5 or 6.
Evidence suggests Tylosaurus was larger at birth compared to other mosasaur genera like Platecarpus and Clidastes.
Unlike most squamates, mosasaurs like Tylosaurus were likely endothermic, or warm-blooded.
Bite marks suggest Tylosaurus also preyed on giant squid and ammonites.
Fossils with injuries inflicted by their own kind suggest Tylosaurus behavior towards each other was mostly aggressive.
Between 3-15% of vertebrae in North American Tylosaurus and 16% in T. bernardi were affected by avascular necrosis.
Tylosaurus proriger was among the largest mosasaurs, with the largest specimens reaching lengths of 12.8 to 13.7 meters.
The size, shape, and spacing of the bite marks on the hadrosaur fossil closely resemble the teeth of Tylosaurus proriger.
The distribution of bite marks on the hadrosaur fossil corresponds inversely to the presence of meat on the animal's body.
Tylosaurus is classified in the family Mosasauridae within the superfamily Mosasauroidea.
The genus Tylosaurus was named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1872.
The genus Tylosaurus belongs to the parent group Tylosaurinae.
Tylosaurus lived between 92 and 66 million years ago during the Turonian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
The oldest known fossil of Tylosaurus is a premaxilla from the Arcadia Park Shale in Texas, dated between 92.1 and 91.4 million years ago.
Edward Drinker Cope persisted in using the genus Liodon for T. nepaeolicus, a species whose type specimen was discovered by Benjamin Franklin Mudge near the Solomon River.
Some researchers argue that the genus Hainosaurus should remain distinct from Tylosaurus based on dental traits.
